newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-TENSE TAYLOR SCORES A HALF CENTURY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TENSE TAYLOR SCORES A HALF CENTURY.

text.p: Mark Taylor scored a timely half century to silence his growing army of critics on Sunday after enduring a tense and bad-tempered second day of Australia's match against Derbyshire.

Test captain Taylor had been pilloried in the Australian media overnight for his first innings failure on Saturday with Greg Chappell, a predecessor as captain, even suggesting he was not in a mentally fit state to lead the tourists.
But he responded with a gritty 59 not out, his first half century in a first class match since scoring 85 against Western Province in Newlands on February 15.
However, Taylor allowed the frustration to temporarily get the better of him by becoming involved in an angry confrontation with a cameraman at the start of the final session.

His anger followed an even more blatant show of dissent from Derbyshire batsman Chris Adams, who was given out lbw to Shane Warne after television replays showed it had hit the bat as Derbyshire declared 87 behind on 275 for nine before Australia reached 148 for two at the close.
Adams was on seven when he pushed Jason Gillespie for a single, only for Warne to make a loud appeal and as he reached the non-striker's end, umpire Vanburn Holder raised his finger.
The Derbyshire batsman, clearly upset at the decision, argued with Holder before trudging off the field, stopping to continue the disagreement with the Australian fielders before finally walking in.
Holder, a former West Indian fast bowler, confirmed he would mention the incident to the England and Wales Cricket Board in his report but conceded he had made a mistake in giving Adams out.

"I thought it hit his pad first and then his bat," explained Holder. "He kept saying he had hit it but he wasn't rude to me. Players have to accept umpire's decisions. Sometimes we are wrong but they have to accept it."
Adams' furious departure summed up a tense second day with Taylor also losing his temper when a cameraman got too close as he came out to bat after the tea interval.

Taylor had been frustrated in his efforts to mastermind his side into a commanding position because his bowlers delivered 34 no-balls and allowed Derbyshire, having resumed on 68 for one, to recover from a mid-order slump following Adams's dismissal.
They slipped from 114 for three to 204 for eight before Andrew Harris and Kevin Dean forged an undefeated 51-run last wicket partnership to help Derbyshire to a respectable total.

Taylor knew that only a major score would prevent an escalation of the recent criticism and he looked visibly relieved when he edged Phil DeFreitas to former Australian colleague Dean Jones at slip in only the second over, only for the Derbyshire captain to miss the straightforward chance.

His nerves were not eased by the loss of opening partner Matthew Elliott who dragged a delivery onto his stumps while Justin Langer was trapped lbw by left-arm seamer Kevin Dean to leave Australia on 35 for two.

But Taylor gradually rediscovered some semblance of form and having hit successive boundaries off Adrian Rollins, beat Michael Bevan to his half century with an off-drive for four off Vince Clarke to claim only his third first class 50 in 18 months.
He progressed to 59 at the close to ensure every leading batsman in the Australian party had made a major score prior to the first Test, while Bevan was unbeaten on 58 having hit six fours.
